entities.title: One shared kit for the web games' online play, scores, page and names
entities.summary: Rally, Hivestorm, Shatterbelt and Samosa carry copies of the same online play, high-score table, page look and name rules, so the explorer shows the same capability, features and state machines three or four times.
acceptanceCriteria: packages/game-kit/ is its own npm project with tests, holding online/ (online.ts), names/ (Samosa's name rules), scores/ (the client's table calls and the Worker's seed, submit, table and scores page, with each game passing in its replay check and table shape) and page/ (look.ts and the signed-in page).
The four games use it, one game per commit, each passing its tests; stored games still pass the replay check; nothing a player sees changes.
changed-games.sh counts a change under packages/ as a change to every game that uses the kit, and ci.yml tests the kit.
One Room and one Seed state diagram, and one capability per shared responsibility, in the kit's .dev folders; the copies are deleted and every link to them repointed.
games/.dev/folder.json no longer says the games share no code, and the create-retro-game web template starts from the kit.

origin.description: The owner asked for a plan to refactor retro-games so that it shows everything the cyberspace explorer can show, and approved its Phase 0.

entities.compromise: The shared code was copied into each game rather than shared, and is kept identical by hand.
entities.cost: A fix in one copy and not the others puts the games out of step without anything saying so, and every view of the shared behaviour is kept up to date four times.

relationships.description: Sharing the file ends the need to check its copies.

entities.title: Link every game's journeys, use cases, features, capabilities and operations
entities.summary: The links between each game's behaviour views have never been checked end to end.
acceptanceCriteria: For each game, each journey links the use cases behind its stages; each use case its features, capability and operations; each feature its capability; each operation its capability; and back.
